But when I -- as I said before, when Avdi came and when I had problems, I started going to the police, and then, out of need, I started doing this business, because raids on my house had become frequent, and the police used to come to the house and raid it. And how could I put up with this? People -- there were people inside, and I was very upset, and people would come and ransack the house. And so I went to the police. Ten policemen coming in, upsetting my brother's children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I had either to work for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. It says here, at the beginning of page 3: "I started to work for the police secretly sometime in 1992 or 1993." Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's just answered that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that same paragraph, you state that one of your relatives was friends with criminals, and in that way, you -- that is how you came to be a police informant, in fact; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please? Because I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning of the paragraph, you say: "Some of the local criminals would rally together and associate with one of my relatives so that I was in a position to offer the police information which could help them to effect certain arrests." So you became an informant on the basis of the information that you had at your disposal through this friend of yours who was friendly with criminals, associated with criminals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "I supplied them with information on local drug dealers and thieves, and the police succeeded in carrying out several good arrests on the basis of the information I supplied them with." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you what the name of that relative was. We'd probably just be wasting our time if we had to go backed to closed session again. But tell me this: When were criminal charges brought against you for the first time? The first time in your life, when were criminal charges brought to bear against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Charges were laid in 1995, when I was held in prison under investigation for nine months in Prishtina. It was a frame-up devised by Avdi, and I was beaten for three hours, and I lost consciousness three times, to confess to a crime I didn't commit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not asking you that. So from 1990 onwards, the criminal charges weren't brought against you. When was the last time they were brought against you, though?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no charges against me, neither first ones nor last ones, just those in 1995. And then there was a gun I had for self-defence. I'm not a criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When were these charges brought against you because of this pistol then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pistol belonged to my father, and he had this gun with a permit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you carried it without a licence to do so, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never carried the pistol at all. This is not true. I never carried it. It was at home. It was hidden in my father's house. I didn't have it on me. I had this pistol with a permit from Mitic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You said it differently a moment ago, but let's move on. On page 3, paragraph 2, you say that in 1995, you escaped to Germany, using your brother's passport; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that year, I escaped to Germany with my brother's passport, and I didn't want to become a SUP informer, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you present yourself falsely to the German authorities or did you tell them that -- your true name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the sake of my security, I presented myself in my brother's name, as it was written in the passport, because I was scared of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you claim that you sought and received asylum in Germany; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I asked for asylum, and I was accepted. And then I returned from Germany because of family problems, because my brother was beaten in the house, and Avdi and the Serbian police were raiding my house every day, and so I returned home just so that there would be no games played with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. How much time went by? How quickly did you return from Germany? I gathered you were in Germany for a short space of time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six months. Six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Six months later; right? Here you say you returned four months later. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After six months, I returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And on the basis of what did you receive asylum in Germany?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got political asylum in Germany because I had problems with the Serbian police. I asked for asylum. I also had a summons, being summoned to the Ferizaj SUP, and on the basis of this, I was given asylum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But the invitation was in your name; right? The summons was in your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The summons was in my brother's name, because I had registered my brother's name in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the passport and the summons were made out in your brother's name, and the summons from the police, too, was in your brother's name and so was the passport; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told you there was a summons, and this younger brother and myself and my cousin, and they came regularly to our house, both to my elder brother and my younger brother. My entire family was summoned to SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's not what I'm asking you. It was in your brother's name that you received your passport and asylum there. And what profession -- what problems did you have in Germany? What problems did you have in Germany?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any kind of problem in Germany. I returned of my own free will. My problems were at home. I spoke with my mother on the telephone. I said, "What's new?" And she told me that the police had been here and had taken my brothers. They would come in the morning. They would come in the evening. They used to go to my aunt, my father's sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's not what I asked you. You provided information to the police about the local drug dealers and thieves. At least, that's what you say in your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, if it's in the statement -- if it's in the statement, you can ask him about it, but it may be that you'll want to move on, because you've got two hours, which is the same time as the Prosecution had to examine this witness, and you've had slightly more than one of those two hours. So you've got another hour -- slightly under an hour left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, first of all, the Prosecution spent far more than two hours, if you count today's time and the time spent in the -- on the last working day. And secondly, this false witness has brought a statement which is 35 pages long. And if you were to read it out loud, we would need at least another one and a half hours to do so because it is densely typed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us get on with it now. I timed the Prosecution. They had 55 minutes on Friday and one hour, six minutes today. That's two hours. Now, you've got slightly under an hour left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would need one and a half hours to read out loud his statement that covers 35 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cover the most important parts and move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From all parts of the statement, you can see that he is a false witness. There is no more important part or most important parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, it says in the statement, and that's why we're wasting time, is that: "I supplied information pertaining to local drug dealers and thieves," and that's what I was asking you about. And you said that the police carried out some good arrests on the basis of that information. Now, my question to you is the following: Did you know when a certain quantity of drugs would be brought in and distributed and who it would be distributed to and when? Does that mean that you knew all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they would -- they discovered some thieves and drug dealers, but how many, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, did you have information of that kind? So you supplied them with information on the basis of facts they knew, when drugs were coming in. Did you deal in drug trafficking yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't. I never was involved in it. It was not my profession. There was nobody in my family involved in that sort of thing. But I did give information about drugs, as I said before, but this was -- this was a small quantity, and it was mainly about robbery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this: Now, you yourself said you were in prison. Which crime were you accused of? Was it robbery or infliction of grievous bodily harm or participation in brawls and beatings? What was the crime that you were imprisoned for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you talking about? Are you talking about 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about what you're talking about when you say that you were in prison. What crime were you in prison for? Were you accused of robbery, grievous bodily harm, beatings, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 1995. I was accused in 1995 of supposedly -- but this was a frame-up. I was accused of beating up somebody called Hajrush from the village of Varrosh who was a collaborator with Avdi Musa, and I supposedly stole 500 marks from him. But this was not true. I got hold of him myself in the corridor when he got out to the toilet, and I found them talking together and in their very -- in front of them, I told them that they were lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's not waste time, please. I'm asking you what crime you were accused of having committed. I'm not asking you what you actually did but what crime were you accused of, because as you say, you spent nine months in prison. On what grounds? Why were you in prison? I suppose you would know that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a frame-up. It was nothing. I did nothing. I was defending myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What he said -- what he said was that he was accused of beating up this man Hajrush.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say you were in prison for nine months. Tell me this, please: How do people from the police force that had you as an informant were not able to help you, especially, as you said, none of this was your fault? So how come they weren't able to help you if you were an informant of theirs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They couldn't help me because they were doing this to me myself. They -- what can I say? They wanted -- they wanted to do it because they didn't like my father. And then there was my father. And then Avdi -- Avdi's idea was merely to destroy my entire family, because my father was against the Serbs. He wasn't just against them. It was like in 1991. He helped the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's not go further than that. You explained that you were necessary to the police, isn't that right, because you worked as their informant. And as they needed you, how come they kept you in prison for nine months? Did they need you or didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I didn't have any information, they didn't need me, and they put me in prison. When I did have information, they didn't put me in prison. And when I sent them information, then they gave me cigarettes, money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Let's move on. We've heard that about the cigarettes, that bit. Now, you got to know somebody nicknamed Crni who was in prison because of armed robbery, as you say; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He was accused of selling arms to someone from Ruga [phoen] from Azem Hajdini Street, with the name Hajdin, and for this reason, he was in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Not to get into specifics, but as it says in your statement, he was in prison for armed robbery. And then you say on page 3, paragraph 5, that before that, for four years, he was in a correction centre in Lipjan; is that right? Before that, he spent four years in a correction centre in Lipjan; right? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this was in 1995, right, when you were in prison with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And four years before that, he spent the whole time in Lipjan in a correction centre; right? And then you go on to say that, before that, he was in the Arkan's Tigers, he was a member of Arkan's Tigers. Now, how can he be in any unit if in 1995 he was in prison with you and had spent the previous four years in the correction centre in Lipjan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Four years -- when he was young, he spent those four years in Lipjan, because he was in the detention centre for juvenile delinquents in Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was our business. We had a bit of money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you where the money came from. Where did you get the money from? I saw the kind of work you did, so where did you get the money to open a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You claim that Mitic gave you cigarettes and that he gave you 100 Deutschmarks each. That is too little money to open a restaurant. Where did you get the rest of the money from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we rented this restaurant, and we gave it -- the rent was 200 marks, and we paid it in instalments, and we just had enough to start up business.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh. For a rent that amounted to 200 Deutschmarks, you had a restaurant. All right, let's move on. In paragraph 4 of page 14, you say that Dejan and you or, rather, Crni and you, as you had put it, sold stolen goods to a man called Srecko from Nis. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the things of Crni. They were the things that were stolen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, but you say that the two of you were selling stolen goods. Now, was theft your source of income? Just give me a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went with them, and I escorted them, but the things belonged to him, not to me. He had stolen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You are trying to say that the fact that you sold stolen goods is something that you wrote in your statement but that's not true, that he was the one who was selling stolen goods and that you were just his friend; are you trying to say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't steal anything. I just accompanied Crni, and he sold the goods. He sold computers and other stuff. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is what you say in paragraph 3, towards the end, on page 14, you say: "I stole a TV set and a cassette player and a video recorder." And then later on, in the next paragraph, you say: "Dejan and I --" that is to say Dejan and you -- "took care of a travel agency." And then in the next sentence: "One night we broke into a store and Dejan stole a fax machine and mobile telephone." And then you say, "Srecko lived in Nis and he bought stolen goods from us and sold them further on in Serbia." And then in the next paragraph, you say that you went to a travel agency by the bus station. "We stole 100 Deutschmarks, five passports, and two telephones." And then in the next paragraph, you came to yet another travel agency by the Serb Orthodox church, and so on and so forth. And then you say that you were stealing, and now you're saying that you were not stealing. I mean, are you a thief or are you not a thief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't robbery in that sense, because it was under the command of the police -- under the order of the police commander. These stores had been financed by the KLA, so we were supposed to go to those stores and vandalise them and destroy everything because they belonged to the Albanians. It wasn't a question of thievery, it was a question of destroying the Albanian shops. That's what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the money that you stole from those shops, you destroyed that money as well; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did. He destroyed things. He burnt the shops. He destroyed, vandalised the shops. That was the order, just to destroy them. It wasn't to steal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you destroy money as well? Did you sell these destroyed goods to Srecko in Nis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said before was that Crni took the stuff and sold it, sold the goods. I didn't take anything. I was only accompanying him, and he did the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. But you wrote in your statement what you did. Tell me, please, did you become a police informer in order to make it easier for yourself to be involved in your own crime? Yes or no. Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did it so that they wouldn't mistreat me, beat me up, because they were -- they had been beating me, sometimes three times a day, every day. They were really beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please. We haven't got much time. Many times in your statement you mention that you were drinking alcohol all the time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, for a person who was almost constantly under the influence of alcohol, you have a very good memory, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can deal with the question in this way: Did the alcohol affect your memory of these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't drink very much alcohol. Maybe a glass, couple of glasses. I wasn't an alcoholic. I drank socially.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But a while ago, you said that you drank a lot, and now you say that you didn't. But this is in line with the course of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't recollect him saying he drank a lot. I may be wrong about that. Yes. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You say that you got orders to burn buses, to burn a shop, et cetera, and that the chief of police gave you these orders and that he had a team that was ready and that they would always establish that the fire was due to faulty installations in the bus, in the shop concerned, et cetera, et cetera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, if his wish was, as you claim, to have this ascribed to KLA operation, why, then, did he have a team that would say that the installations were faulty? Wasn't it logical then for the team to say that this was done by the KLA, not that it was due to faulty installations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the stores, they said it was the electrical installations, whereas the buses, they said that emblems and writing of the KLA were found so that they could say that the KLA did it. Whereas for the shops it was the electrical installations. The buses, it was the emblems of the KLA were found near the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the letter. The letter is a different thing. I'm not asking you about the letter. You also said in connection with the buses that the police team that was prepared by your instructions-giver said what they said, and you said the same thing about the buses too. You also referred to faulty installations. So -- all right. This is quite clear. And as for this, whether he drank constantly, I'm just going to mention to you what he said in the statement. Thirty-five pages long the statement is. On page 8, paragraph 2, he says: "For a while, the three of us took -- stayed there and ate and drank." And then, "I was a bit drunk that night because Dragan kept paying drinks for me." Page 9, paragraph 4: "At 10.00, I went to Nacional and we had beer." And then page 9, paragraph 7: "So we stayed there, drinking." The same night, paragraph 8 on page 9: "We went to our restaurant. We had a couple of drinks each and then we left." And then page 10, paragraph 4: "We went there and then we watched TV and drank." Page 11 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he's -- you've made the point, and he's given his explanation. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Page 13, paragraph 4: "As a matter of fact, they saw us one night as we were returning home, drunk." Et cetera, et cetera. There's not a single page on which you do not mention that you were drinking alcohol and that you were drunk. So are you an alcoholic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's dealt with that. He's given his explanation. There's no need for it to be repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did drink, but I was drinking with the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no need for it to be repeated. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As for the installations, you wrote here quite nicely, that is 9/4, 10/11, 12, et cetera, "due to faulty installations." That's what you wrote here. It's on page 9 the fourth paragraph, on page 10 the third paragraph, on page 11 the first paragraph. So you always say that, upon police instructions, you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us -- let us -- just one moment. There's an objection, and then we'll deal with this question. Yes, Ms. Romano.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. We'll redact it. The point -- the point that was being made, Witness K5, is this: If it was the purpose to ascribe these various crimes to the KLA, if that was the purpose of the police, can you assist us as to why, when investigations were carried out, they were reported as accidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the stores were reported as accidents. For example, in Manastirc, several times the crimes were -- were attributed to the KLA. And in the village of Nerodime, there were two grenades. And in Klina, they said that the KLA had done it because the KLA had that type of arms, the Chinese weapons. And at Manastirc, it was done that way when the emblems of the KLA were left there, in Albanian. And they told the journalists in Shtime e Re to come out and speak Albanian -- or people to come out and rob the journalists who were there, speaking Albanian. But that wasn't done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. As for the buses, you say that you did not say that it was a question of installations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh. I didn't have any interpretation. So not for the buses. Then I'm going to read a sentence out to you. Page 9, paragraph 3: "When the police carried out an on-site investigation, Mitic's men, it was concluded that the fire was due to faulty installations on the bus." That's what it says in your statement, but now you do not recall what the statement says and what your claim is. So you informed on the Albanians. You were saying who was assisting the KLA, who was in the KLA, who was cooperating with the KLA. Am I right or am I not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I said. I didn't say who was a member of the KLA or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. But that's what you were saying just awhile ago. Let's not waste time. On page 5 of your statement -- I'm going on. I am going on. You say here, on the last paragraph on page 5: "I identified several cafes and restaurants in Urosevac. I want --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The accused is reading this too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You'll have to read more slowly, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here: "I identified several restaurants" as you said that, "It was I who identified persons from pictures who worked for the KLA, who did not work for the KLA." So you keep using the first person singular all the time. Why did you want that? Why did you want that? "I want a bomb to be thrown into this cafe." "I want a bomb to be thrown at the Casablanca Cafe." Why did you want that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't want it. It was Mitic who had the list of Albanian coffeeshops that we were supposed to bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's clear, but I asked you about what you wrote here, because you say, "I want this," "I want that." Did you perhaps throw these bombs into the cafes owned by persons from whom you were taking racket money? And then you threw bombs into their cafes when they didn't want to pay up. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one matter. I don't want to -- the part of the paragraph should be misled. I think that it's very clear when he says, "I want to throw it," "I want to do that," he's mentioned the list. Maybe it is a translation problem, but what he says is, "The list is as follows," and then he mentioned all the list. That is page 6 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, I have it. It's not very clear. In any event, the witness has given his answer to the allegation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, when was this meeting held in March when you were allegedly with Crni, Mitic, and, as you call him, Bogic Bogi? When you all went to Pristina together. These are pages 4, 5, 6 of your statement. On which date was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but it was in 1998 when we went to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, it was in 1998 that you went to Pristina. All right. You know the year. And can you give at least one precise date concerning any one of the events that you have been describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you any dates, no. I wasn't interested in noting down dates at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's now time for --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now time for the adjournment. It's 12.15. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time do I have left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will consider that during the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I have a lot of questions, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've got half an hour more. That will give you over two hours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means how much time do I have left as from now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You did not answer my question as to whether you threw bombs at the property of people that your group was extorting money from. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You say that you had a letter that was given to you by Mitic and that was allegedly supposed to give you protection from the police, and you say it had a stamp of the Belgrade police and Mitic's signature. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you claim that Mitic said to you that you shouldn't show this letter to anyone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- in Ferizaj, he told me not to show it to anyone in Ferizaj, not elsewhere, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you were in Urosevac. So how did you have the opportunity of getting protection from that letter if you were not allowed to show that letter to anyone, if that's what he said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not supposed to show it to anyone in Ferizaj, to the police in Ferizaj if anyone stopped me. But in Viti or in Gjilan, if I were in danger and if there were policemen and they asked me, in the market square, for example, if they asked me, "Why are you here? What are you doing?" And if they wanted to take me to the substation and wanted to beat me up, I could show it, I could show the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many policemen saw you and Crni coming to Mitic's office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Vladi who was a storekeeper, a warehouse-keeper whom I knew was an informer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So other policemen did not see you, then, when you came to the office.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, no, but in 1999, yes. There were other policemen there at that time with Mitic, which I mentioned earlier. But the Albanians didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But if so many policemen and inspectors saw you coming to his office, then what was the point of you not showing the letter to anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in danger in Ferizaj from the police. I had problems if -- it was the problems with Avdi were the problems. If they asked why I'd come to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you were not in danger there. You and Dejan, after the burning of the bus, allegedly agreed that you would no longer socialise in public. That is what you claim; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. You say that after the burning of the shop, you spent the night in the car that was parked nearby; is that right? That is to say, until about 5.00 or 5.30, you were asleep. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What event are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you say that after the burning of the shop, you spent the night at the car that was parked nearby. You say that you were asleep until 5.00 or 5.30.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on because time is limited. This is what it says in your statement, though. On page 13, in paragraph 3, you say that: "In Urosevac, there was some group called Crna Ruka that was operating there; is that right? The Black Hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 4 on page 13, you say that soon people started talking that you and Dejan were the Black Hand and that you were killing people for money. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this alleged phantom Black Hand killed for money, and it could have included Albanians if they included you, as an Albanian, amongst them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't any Albanians in that group. It belonged to the Serb police. It was called the Black Hand. They were -- they were to be found in every town in Kosova, in Prishtina, Suhareka, Rahovec, Prizren, Ferizaj. But it was the group from Ferizaj, from Fekija [phoen], there was a Dragan Jashovic who summoned me, who called me to find out who were the members of the Black Hand there. They came because the members came to our coffeeshop. Later during the war, in 1999, the Black Hand joined with the other forces, with Dimitri. There was also a policeman from Nerodime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The citizens said that you and Dejan were members of that Black Hand. How, then, was it possible, if they believed that you were the Black Hand, that the KLA, after the war, arrested you and released you, although -- if they believed that you were a member of the Black Hand, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had information and had doubts about me because they knew normally there weren't any Albanians in that organisation, and so why would I be involved? So they had doubts as to me and, as I said earlier, they took me and interrogated me for three days. But they didn't beat me. They didn't want to defend me. No one wanted to defend me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But as you yourself say, the KLA killed Albanians if there was the slightest suspicion that they were loyal to the Serbian authorities. But they didn't kill you, for whom the Albanians thought you were a member of the Black Hand. Don't you appear to yourself to be ridiculous when you claim what you do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter for comment. No need to answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who the KLA killed or not. That was their own affair. I wasn't -- I didn't have anything to do with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. The -- you did the Tai Chi or coffee-shop, tea shop near the mosque yourself and looted it. What did you steal from this tea house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order came from Mitic for me to go to the tea shop belonging to Fatmir in Ferizaj. I'd seen a photograph of it. Mitic had seen a photograph of it, of karate players in Ferizaj near the centre, and there was a store there, a company, and Mitic was of the opinion that all these companies were being financed by the KLA, and told me to burn them all down, all these companies financed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My question was: What did you steal from the tea house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They gave me the key. Mitic gave me the key. There were 50 keys, in fact. And I used the keys and got into the tea shop. Tried the first key, the second key, the third key, the tenth key. And then I took the pictures, and I took out everything else, took the -- and I took the photographs and took them back to the police and to Mitic, these photographs. There was a Sladjan Staljinovci, and I took the photographs to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K5, did you steal anything? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. It says differently in the statement, but I'll leave that to others to see too. Now, you and Dejan did several travel agencies too, as you say. Now, how much money did you steal from those travel agencies and what kind of goods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he took. I don't know how much money he took. I don't know because I didn't go into the building. I was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in your statement, you say that you and he looted those travel agencies, and now you say you weren't inside. When were you telling the truth, before, later on, or is anything that you're saying the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looted the travel agency. That's true. I told exactly what I did and what I heard. But he was the one who did the job. I was just with him. I was a friend. He looted and destroyed the premises. I can tell you what was done at the tea shop, how I got into that building with the key and took the photographs. That was what I did. But the building -- the business of burning -- of killing Albanians, of burning and looting shops, that was another thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You say you wanted to release some snakes in the mosque prior to the prayers there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. That came from Mitic, the order, during -- during ceremonies in the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. How many snakes did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't do the job, carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't have any snakes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't even ask to get any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say you saw the army shoot down three NATO aeroplanes near Urosevac. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were planes, observer -- observer planes to observe the terrain. They were planes without pilots.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. They say they didn't. Now, who's telling the truth, you or NATO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter of comment. The witness has said -- the witness has said what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Saw them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- and we can't take the matter any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did NATO bomb Urosevac? You were there throughout the war; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me briefly, on what date did you take your family to the railway station in order to leave Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Roughly. Tell us roughly then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I can't remember. How can I tell you something I can't remember? And then you accuse me of lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What year did your family leave Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it wartime then or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was killed by the NATO bombing in Urosevac? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was killed. I know they attacked the army barracks there, and they were -- there was a tank which was destroyed. I saw the tank myself. And in other villages where the army was present, there were attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what happened to the members of the State Security Service, the Albanians and you say -- as you say Sulejman from Jezerc, Hismet Pali [phoen] from Urosevac, Bajram Luri; what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left the country. Each one went in his own direction to a third country. Luri, I don't know. He isn't in Ferizaj. I don't know what happened to him, I didn't see him any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you claim that Bajram's sister works for NATO and Bajram for the DB, the security service, is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Bajram Luri worked for the Serbian security in Ferizaj. He was an interpreter in Ferizaj and in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 18, last paragraph, you state that you discovered to the Serb policemen members -- the identities of the members of the KLA. Sadik Bega nicknamed Mortaje from Jezerc was one of them. Jeton, nicknamed Toni from Talinovac, Arijan from Urosevac, Roboti from Balic, and Simpo Ruzdi from Urosevac, a director of the PTT in Urosevac and Ekrem Baliu in whose house the members of the KLA held the Serbs they'd kidnapped; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention that, but the inspector knows himself. Dragan Jashovic discovered that inside. I did know a lot of people in the KLA, but I didn't mention them, didn't disclose their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, these are names that you quoted. Now, what about these Serbs; were they taken to the KLA prison that was in Klecka near Lipjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I've heard reports about them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what happened to those Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I heard about that from Crni, that people were taken, civilians. The Serbs took them to Klecka, but they are rumours. I didn't see anything, but Crni had some friend who was involved in the village of Nerodime. Zuti was his name, and he was a member of Arkan's group in Bosnia during the war. And they took Bazel. They had arms with them, that's what Crni told me. And they blocked the -- the KLA had blocked the army there, had blocked off the army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 19, last paragraph -- on page 19, last paragraph, you say: "We started drinking Johnnie Walker whiskey." So you remember the brand of the whiskey that you drank but you don't remember a single date that is relevant to your testimony and statement. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You don't have to answer that. That's just a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 21, in the first paragraph, you claim that they gave you a pistol of some kind but you didn't know whether there was any ammunition in it or not. Did you ever learn whether there was any ammunition in the pistol or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the beginning, I -- I understood that there was, in 1998. But in 1999, I was frightened that there would be no real munition for this pistol. I was scared. I -- I had some in 1998. I tried it at home to try and find out whether it was real ammunition or not, because I thought they were playing a trick on me. But in 1999, I didn't believe them any more because they took the pistol away from me in 1998 and gave it back to me in 1999, and I thought they may well have taken the bullets away. And I had a permit for this pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you had a permit for the pistol that they gave you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You established that it was loaded and that the ammunition was the right one. And on what date did you perform these operations that you claimed to have performed, blowing up houses and burning houses in Nezir Beqiri, the motel in Gimi? Tell me exactly when that was, what date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the dates, but it was in 1999. There were -- those matters that I told you about earlier in 1998 and these houses of Agim and Yzdri Beqiri and others were in 1999, as I said, not done by me but by the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 24, you claim that you got drunk. Do you remember what you had drank drunk on that occasion because you got drunk once again? You say, "We all started drinking." What were you drinking then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at SUP on that day and we drank brandy. They were all drinking and I drank with them too. It's true that I was drinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You say here that you were drinking plum brandy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of brandy it was, but it was some kind of brandy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. On page 26, last paragraph, you say Mitic told you that you had to take care of Jusuf. What date was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you about the dates; I don't really remember. This happened in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you don't remember the date, although you do remember that, as you were very drunk, as you yourself say, that Mitic called you up at 1300 hours and that Musa and Haliti came to see you at 10.00; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What date was that then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. On page 27, second paragraph, this is what you say: "I entered the restaurant, the Pranvera restaurant, and sat down. There was a well in the restaurant with a cover to it, and on the cover was a belt and some tobacco, and when I went inside, I could see steps leading downwards into the cellar. I saw that there were a lot of people there and realised that the police were using the cellar as a prison." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true. And there were people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't that the same thing, the same one? What does "Pranvera" mean in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pranvera" means "pranvera," "spring." In Albanian, "spring" is "Pranvera."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And in the statement, you talk about yourself and him, and a moment ago in answer to my question, when I asked you about the property -- who the Pranvera restaurant belonged to, you said that people didn't know that it was in fact your restaurant, that it belonged to you. That's what you said. Now, are you claiming now that it wasn't a restaurant owned by you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What he said was that it was a different restaurant. There were two restaurants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: (redacted) established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, you've got two minutes left, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say members of the KLA beat you for three months with wires, baseball bats, that they stamped their feet on you, that they would make pauses, give you cigarettes, then beat you on the soles of your feet, et cetera, et cetera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were really KLA or not. I said before that they pretended to be members of the KLA and said they were members of the KLA, but they asked me about other problems. But the KLA took me at the beginning, and they took me from my uncle and kept me for three days, and they didn't beat me. And I'm not frightened of them or anybody else. They didn't beat me. They gave me cigarettes and bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. You've already explained that. But that was the second time. Let me remind you. On page 33, you say they came wearing KLA uniforms. Now, all this was after the war. "They took me to a cellar with dark windows. There were baseball bats, the handles of axes. All of them were masked except for a fat guy with grey hair who said he was from Skopje and had killed a lot of Albanians who had collaborated with the Serbs. He cocked a pistol at me and said that I had to tell him everything that I did. He was the only one without a mask and I can recognise him. They questioned me and then began beating me with a wire. They tied my feet, placed me on the ground. One of them stepped on my chest, took my shoes and socks off. They took my shoes off. They made pauses, gave me cigarettes. When they thought that I would lose consciousness, they threw water over me, and kept me like that for three months, beating me constantly. One day, I looked through the window and saw that I was in the village of Slatina, the Kacanik municipality." Is that true or is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that they took me, but once again, they weren't members of the KLA. They were thieves. They were a gang from Kacanik. They took me because of my family, because I had my wife from Kacanik. And they took me because of problems with my wife. I had problems before that over this issue, and they exploited the issue to use the name of the KLA. And they took me to Sllatina and beat me and held me for three months there. But I know these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K5 -- Mr. Milosevic, you've got one question which you can ask. One more and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have I understood you correctly? Just tell me this: Did I understand you to say that some NATO officers suggested that you should form a group of people and arm them and fight against the KLA who wanted to kill you? That's what it says in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you chose not to fight but to flee to Macedonia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't run away from the KLA. I've got nothing to run away from because the KLA didn't beat me. And even if I see them today, I would stretch out my hand for them, because they only kept me for three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K5, you've dealt with all that. Now, are there any questions from the amicus?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Witness, would you assist the Court in answering a few questions I would put to you. Avdi Musa, he was a Kosovar Albanian, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In 1990, 1991, the political situation in Kosovo changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And Albanian police officers were removed from the police force; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Now, you gave evidence that Musa returned and was appointed police commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When did Musa return to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that before or after the situation changed in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it changed not when he came but when there were Serbs in all positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How come that an Albanian Kosovar was appointed in an office of police commander after the situation changed, as you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was on the side of the Serbs, and they wanted to appoint him captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When Musa was killed, why did you not cease your activities as informant of the police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Musa was killed after the war, when all this business was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I see. Have you heard of other Albanian Kosovars who were collaborating with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard that there were some, but I don't know the names. But these people didn't work as inspectors. They worked for salaries. But these other people, these people were framed, and they were put in difficult positions and -- and then they said, "Help me and nobody will dare touch you," because no Albanians worked with the police from their own free will but only under duress.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Whatever the cause may be, you've heard about others who cooperated, collaborated with the Serbs, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard that somebody killed them, but I -- who, I don't know. I don't really know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you heard -- have you heard about ill-treatment of these people besides killings, or arresting these people besides killings, or beating up these people besides killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have heard, but I've never seen anything of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever been attacked by other Albanian Kosovars, relatives of witness -- of victims because of your work for the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Now I'm scared of them, and my -- word has got around that I was working for them. But they haven't attacked me, nor did the KLA, only this gang that took me to Sllatina has caused me problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever been threatened by Albanian Kosovars, relatives of victims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told the Court you have been questioned by the KLA twice. Have you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you told --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the real KLA took me, and they held me for three days. And the second time --

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There's no need to repeat that. The second time, you said that these were not the real KLA. When you were questioned about that by the Prosecution, you gave an answer, "I do not understand," and I read your answer, so please listen carefully. The Prosecution asked you: "Q. Witness, how do you know they were merely a group and not KLA?" Your answer was: "A. I could understand this because the KLA, before they came, and they wanted information, but the other group -- but the other group was asking me about other problems which I had beforehand because of my wife and other problems of this kind." Now, what do you mean by problems you had beforehand because of your wife and other problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By this, I wanted to say that these people were not from the KLA, because I had been with them. But these people came dressed as the KLA, but they weren't members of the KLA. They were a gang. They stole things, looted things, and killed people. I don't know about this, but this is what I've heard of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Why do you refer to problems because of your wife and other problems? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say that I was married, and I had a wife from Kacanik, and I had problems with a person when I went out with my wife. He was from Kacanik. And according to what I think and also the questions they asked me, this was the problem that was involved. They didn't interrogate me about anything. They just asked me things in order to beat me. They didn't want any kind of real information from me. Just -- just ridiculous questions. These were not real questions. They only wanted to beat me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And that for a period of three months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I think, I didn't give you dates, but I think it was about three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In a previous statement, you did not tell anything about the persons who interrogated you not being KLA. Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say so because nobody asked me. And now that you're asking me, I'm explaining. They were in the KLA uniforms. But before, nobody asked me. But now I'm answering at greater length, and I'm saying that they were in KLA uniforms and with weapons, and they took me and beat me, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. From the transcript, it appears that the Prosecution did not ask you about that. You raised the issue that these were not KLA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So I ask you again: Since it was not raised by any question, you brought it up, why didn't you tell that in your first interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not all that interesting. It didn't seem to me to be crucial. They -- I told them that they -- that the KLA took me and interrogated me for three days and got some information from me, but -- but I didn't -- I didn't tell them -- the other people, I didn't tell anything, but I told the KLA about Dejan and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you report to the KLA that imposters arrested you and mistreated you for a period of time, claiming that they were KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't report it to the KLA. I reported it to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: After you were released, did you see a doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in hospital in Skopje, and I have the document here. I don't have it with me, but I do have the document. And I had an operation, and I had severe trauma. I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does the document say about your injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document says that I was mistreated, and I was tortured and that I experienced trauma. Not exactly trauma but headache and hurt -- pain in the kidneys and pain in the legs. And after a time, I was in intensive care for a while. I was three days in Skopje. There was something inside my lungs, too. There was something that had burst, a vein or something, and the doctor noted that this had come from my mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did the report indicate any scars on your body because of burning cigarettes on your body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- I cut myself with a broken bottle, but I couldn't -- couldn't ensure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I'm afraid that is not an answer to my question. Were there any scars found on your body because of burning cigarettes on your body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't burn me with cigarettes. No. Nobody burned me with cigarettes. I was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You do realise that you said in your previous statement that you were burned by cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Perhaps somebody did burn me, but I don't know. I only know that, yes, I do, I do have marks of what was done to me, but I can't -- I don't really want to think of this any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Since people were suspecting you of assisting the Serb police since people saw you together with someone who was suspected to be a member of the Black Hand, since rumours spread around your involvement with Black Hand, how come you were not killed the second time you were arrested by these people who you say were gangsters, not KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they didn't ask me about the Black Hand. I said this before. They asked me about problems that I had. They only wanted to beat me up. There was nothing else involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And why didn't the KLA kill you the first time when they arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I wasn't beaten by the KLA the first time. Because I had no blood on my hands. I never killed Albanians. I haven't killed people. I have come here to say that my hands are not stained in blood. And anybody -- does anybody have any documents or facts to show this? Has anybody come -- told me to come here? But because -- I've come here because I know that I never did anything. If I had done, I wouldn't be here. I wouldn't have dared even leave my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you tell, in these three days you were kept by the KLA, what you told the Court here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And they released you after having told them what you told the Court here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any information of this kind. I didn't have very much information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I'm asking you, did you tell --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter requests the witness to repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they took me for three days, they didn't have the information. They had information that I was with the Serbs, had been with the Serbs, and that I was involved in the Black Hand organisation. This involvement, they asked me about it. They said, "Do you have that car? Were you in that car? Were you there?" They brought in witnesses. They asked did anyone see me there with them. And if they had found someone, they would have said, "Well, we have witnesses who saw you." But then they realised I didn't have any links with the Black Hand and let me go. They took me into a car and took me to my maternal uncle's and said, "You are free now from the KLA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Now, let me phrase it in this way: Did you tell the KLA in these three days what you told the Court these days, or did you lie to them by not disclosing what your real involvement was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell them, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you lied to the questions of them, hiding away what your real involvement was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't lie to them. It was about the burning, about the cars burning, about buses, stores. They asked me, "Are you involved in the Black Hand organisation?" That was what they asked. "Did you know certain people? Did you have that car? Did you own that car?" They thought I belonged to the Black Hand. But they didn't ask about other things. It wasn't that I didn't -- I didn't lie to them. It's just they didn't ask about certain things. And then later I was at the Red Cross and gave information. The Red Cross took me back home and took me somewhere else, off somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Witness, you testified earlier about the work that you did for Mitic and the Serbian police and also that this work involved activities as theft, arson, and exploding buildings, and trying to attempt the liquidation of people. Have you heard rumours during that time that there were criminal charge or reports made against you for this very illegal fact and act that you were doing and were ordered to do by the police and by Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? Because I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. You testified that you worked for Mitic and that you did several acts like robbery, theft, and attempt to liquidation. You were involved and you participated in these acts. At that time, have you heard rumours among the population that there were charges or there were reports against you for these very illegal acts that you were doing for Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't do this sort of thing. I said before my order was only to point out houses. Dejan and the Serbian police were involved in this sort of thing. I was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness K5, that's not the question which you were asked. The question which the Prosecutor asked you was whether you heard any rumour that during that time there were charges against you for what you did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I never heard of any such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Have you heard any rumours about you or about the work you were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: When you report back to Mitic, did he ever ask you to go out and check with the population what the people were talking about regarding the acts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: What were the comments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we did a job, for instance, blowing up a motel like Agim's motel, after the job was done, I would go to the police at Bankkos, and I would go to Mitic dressed in plainclothes, and Mitic would say, "Go and find out what the rumours are, who they say do these things." And I would go out and talk to people. And some people would say the police has done it. But people didn't know who had done it, people would just say the police had done. They would say Arkan's men have done it, something like that. These were the rumours and I'd send the information to Mitic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Have you ever heard any rumour or any comment that you were involved in these activities or that you were doing such things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People have talked. I said before, people talked, and they -- they said about me that I too took part in this sort of activity, in the Black Hand. There were rumours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And have you ever been in prison before 1999? Had you ever been in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was, in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And before that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Have you ever been notified of any charges against you or have you ever been in any trial for any charges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know of any other procedure. And on that business of that fight with the Gypsy, I was beaten but -- and then also I was detained for nine months when I had that fight with Hajrush in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Witness -- sorry. Witness, early on, you also testified that in 1995, when you were arrested, you spent some time in prison, nine months, and you mentioned that you confessed for something that you did not -- did not commit. Can you explain to the Court exactly what happened in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1995, I was in a cafe, and there came a collaborator of Avdi Musa into the cafe, with a pseudonym Bajgora, and his friend Hajrush Rrusha from the village of Varrosh, and came to provoke me, and I defended myself and I beat this person. And he beat me and then I beat him. And on the next day, they came, this was Avdi Musa, Dragan, Lubisha, and then there was a car, a 101, a white 101, and took me to the police, to the third floor, to Avdi's office. And going out to the toilet, I saw Hajrush and Azem and Avdi talking. And -- and he said -- and they asked him did I know this person, and they wanted to -- and they started to beat me because I didn't admit to beating him up. And they told me that they would give me 500 marks to admit, but I didn't admit, and that is why they beat me up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: So did you confess?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you ask again?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Did you confess or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confessed under duress.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: And after your trial, were you acquitted or convicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My Judge was Danica Marinkovic, and I went in court in front of her, and my lawyer was Ymer Rovci and the court released me as innocent, and my lawyer said that I could seek compensation. But I didn't do this. I said I didn't want money.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. This happened in 1995, right after you came back from Germany, when you escaped to Germany. Do you believe, Witness, that -- or it's correct to say that this could be a type of retaliation because you escaped and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's not for the witness to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Just I'll rephrase the question. That happened right after you came back from Germany; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was maybe two days afterwards. They came immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, was Mitic aware of the fact that during the time you were doing the work for him, that you stole things and you kept some of the things, you and the other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But Mitic gave the orders himself. Not directly to steal, but before, as I said, Dejan did this kind of thing, and I kept him company. He knew everything, he told us himself to do these things. He had -- it was my job to point out that this is so-and-so's shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Romano, just a minute. At this time, since I have noted that the accused and amicus cited the witness statement several times, I think it's better to exhibit the statement now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to ask this at the end of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which will be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I'd like to ask the question regarding the -- what was said just now. Mr. K5, in your statement on page 14 in the English version, at paragraph 4, do you remember that you wrote like this, I quote -- it's about the tearoom near the mosque: "Mitic told me to rob the shop and keep everything for myself, just bring the photograph to him." Is it true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true that he said that. He wanted the photograph. Everything else, I destroyed, as I said earlier. I just took the photographs and took them to him, and the other things I destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But later, at the same paragraph, you wrote: "I stole a television, tape player, and a video player." Is it true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to stealing, I had a specific order. I destroyed the things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Witness, although the investigations were orchestrated by Mr. Mitic, they concluded that the stores, they were burned or destroyed due to electrical installations or accidents, when you went back to talk to the population, asked by Mitic to check out what were the comments and what they were saying, what did they think happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their opinion was that it must have been the police. Some thought it was the police. Some thought it was thieves. There were different -- different opinions as to what might have happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Why did they think it was the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the police did do such -- carry out such activities, did robberies, carried out robberies in Ferizaj among people's houses, private Albanian homes. The police were involved in such skulduggery.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Witness, when asked by Mr. Wladimiroff, you claim that the people who detained you for three months, they were not KLA. Let's assume they were KLA or they could have been KLA, just as a chance that they might have been KLA.
