Was it understandable that the KLA, because the work you did as an informant and the bad things that you did for the Albanians, was it understandable that the KLA wanted to detain, interrogate, or even maltreated you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Have you ever mentioned in your statement or -- that you have been burnt with cigarettes by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really don't remember. I'm not sure whether I could assert that or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Did it happen? Were you burned with cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, you must bring this to a close.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Ms. Romano.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: It is in fact a correction that I would like to make, but I need to do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In Doctor -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps the matter which you raised just now of the new document, you can put some -- if you have some suggestions as to what should be done, or any application, you could put it into writing so we could have it overnight to consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The other short administrative matter relates to part of the testimony of Dr. Baccard. I know that the Court won't have his report with it, but on page 19 of 154 pages, under Racak, there is reference to a witness statement. I needn't give the name of the witness concerned, but there's a witness statement that he referred to. The matter is covered in the testimony on pages of transcript that I've got available for distribution, but it's pages 5288 to 5290 and 5305 to 5308. So those are available for you to remind you of what was said. The witness statement itself was not included in the Racak binder because expectations as to whether that person will be giving evidence were such that it wasn't necessary to put it in the binder. In the event the person hasn't given evidence, then it would appear that the statement for the particular and narrow purposes identified by Dr. Baccard should now be an exhibit and should be added to the binder, but I thought I should give you a chance to consider that matter by looking at the raw material before we do it or we seek to do it. So those transcripts are available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Before we close, Mr. Milosevic, you wanted to raise something about some exhibits for the last witness. Have you got them available?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You haven't got the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you wish me to give it to you now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you can hand them in, so much the better. Yes, we can have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. First with respect to the question of Rugova's party and the LDK, that in 1990 it considered that it should take part in the elections in Serbia but that it assessed that it wouldn't be getting more places in parliament than the 15 it had at the time. And I'm handing in a document which the opposing side gave under the title of "Rugova on the Democratic Platform of Kosovo." This is the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm afraid time is against us. We can't hear anything. But if you've got any documents, perhaps you could just hand them in and we'll consider them for tomorrow. Or we'll have to go on with this tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are the exhibits which you requested. You said would I be good enough to provide them, and I'm now explaining to you what they're about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm afraid we haven't -- we haven't time for explanations because our time -- our time in the courtroom is up. So if you could just hand the documents in. But if you want to explain them, you must do it tomorrow. Do whichever you want. Witness K5, thank you for coming to give evidence. It's now over. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will now adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of May, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
